sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the path segment of the matching endpoint. getUserByEmail checks the address against TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, a deliberately loose shape rule, one @ with non-empty whitespace-free parts, and refuses anything else before dispatch. getUsers takes an optional project and addresses get_users/{project_id} when it is given. updateGroup injects the path identifier into the body as group_id, overwriting whatever the caller supplied, because TestRail rejects a body without it. No write payload is parsed by a public method, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

UserSchema is the reply shape and is permissive: role_id, is_admin, group_ids and the enterprise fields are all nullish because older servers omit them and get_current_user returns a reduced record, and mfa_required admits an integer because TestRail Cloud wire-encodes it as 0 or 1. UserAddPayloadSchema requires a non-empty name and an email checked with TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, the lookup's shape rule, which UserUpdatePayloadSchema applies to its optional email as well; addUser and updateUser forward the payload unparsed, so the boundary applies it. It declares role_id, group_ids and assigned_projects as positive integers; UserUpdatePayloadSchema makes every field optional. GroupSchema carries id, name and a nullish user_ids. AddGroupPayloadSchema requires name; UpdateGroupPayloadSchema makes it optional and its comment records that TestRail accepts an empty update body. RoleSchema carries id, name, is_default and a nullish is_project_admin.

TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN is the user email shape rule, exactly one @ with non-empty, whitespace-free local and domain parts, shared by the get_user_by_email lookup and both user write payloads. Its comment records that single-label domains and domain literals are legitimate on self-hosted, LDAP, AD and SSO instances and that authoritative format validation is TestRail's.
zObject uses passthrough, so the declared payload types admit unknown properties; the MCP boundary must reject them separately.

get_user and get_user_by_email return one user, the latter taking the address as a query parameter. get_users returns an array and accepts an optional project in the path; from TestRail 6.6 only administrators may omit it, and the project form omits inactive users, omits users holding only global access, and reports each role at its project level. add_user requires name and email and accepts is_active, is_admin, role_id, group_ids, mfa_required, email_notifications, sso_enabled and assigned_projects, with is_active defaulting to false; update_user supports the same fields. The reference's get_current_user section contradicts the endpoint's own purpose by listing a required user_id parameter while describing the user making the request.

input_policy.notes: One of the endpoints with no path segment: everything is in the body. The driver does not parse this payload, so every rule here is the boundary's alone, including the address format, which is the driver's declared one restated with the Unicode flag this server requires and held to the driver's own verdicts by a test.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the created user in the get_user format; entity-field drift is advisory.

parameters.semantics: The user's full name, which TestRail requires. No coercion; TestRail owns the format.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Accept a string.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.

parameters.semantics: The user's address, which TestRail requires. The boundary checks only its shape, exactly one @ with non-empty whitespace-free parts on either side, the rule the driver applies to get_user_by_email, so a single-label domain or domain literal, which a self-hosted, LDAP, AD or SSO instance legitimately stores, reaches TestRail, which owns the authoritative rule. The driver's write payload declares the same rule, TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, but addUser forwards the payload unparsed, so the boundary applies it. No coercion and no trimming.
